name: Centro
tagline: The compact grid where daily life happens
description: Pucon's downtown is a small, walkable grid anchored by Avenida O'Higgins, packed with cafes, tour operators, supermarkets, and most short-term rentals. Everything you need day to day is within a 10 to 15 minute walk, making it the default base for remote workers without a car. It gets loud and crowded in peak summer but stays convenient year-round.
bestFor: first-time visitors and car-free remote workers who want everything close
pros: Walk to cafes, shops, and bus terminal
Most rental options and short-term listings
Best wifi and cellular coverage in town
cons: Loud and crowded in summer high season
Limited parking if you do have a car

name: Playa Grande (Lakefront)
tagline: Black-sand beach living, steps from downtown
description: The lakefront strip along Playa Grande sits just south of Centro, where the town meets the black volcanic sand shore of Lake Villarrica. Rentals here trade a few minutes of extra walking distance for direct lake and volcano views, and it's a favorite for morning swims or evening walks. Still close enough to downtown to feel connected rather than isolated.
vibe: scenic, relaxed, slightly quieter than Centro
bestFor: people who want lake views and easy beach access without leaving town
pros: Quieter than the main grid at night
Still a short walk to Centro's cafes and shops
cons: Fewer rental options than Centro proper
Can get crowded with day-tripping tourists in summer

name: Camino Villarrica-Pucon Strip
tagline: The residential corridor between the two towns
description: The road connecting Pucon to Villarrica, roughly 25 km away along the lake, is lined with residential subdivisions, cabanas, and longer-term rental homes that offer more space and quiet than the town centres. It suits people who want a car and don't mind a short drive for groceries or coworking, trading convenience for privacy and often better value.
bestFor: longer-term stays, families, or anyone wanting more space and lower rent
pros: More space and privacy than downtown rentals
Generally better value per square meter
Easy access to both Pucon and Villarrica
cons: Requires a car for daily errands and work spots
Limited public transit along the corridor

name: Caburgua
tagline: A turquoise lake village 25 minutes from Pucon
description: The small village of Caburgua sits beside its own strikingly turquoise lake, about a 25 to 30 minute drive northeast of Pucon toward the Argentine border. It's a quieter, more rural alternative for people who want genuine nature immersion, waterfalls, and lakeside cabanas, at the cost of being fully dependent on a car and far from any coworking or dense amenities.
bestFor: nature-focused remote workers who don't mind isolation and driving into town for supplies
pros: Stunning turquoise lake and nearby waterfalls
Very quiet and low tourist density outside summer
Lower cabana rental prices than Pucon centre
cons: No meaningful wifi infrastructure or coworking
Fully car-dependent for groceries and errands
Very limited dining and services locally
